headline: Global News Tonight: France Protests, Public Health and Political Accountability
summary: RadiantWaves Media brings you a global news update for Sunday, 25 October 2026. France is facing renewed pressure following large demonstrations over living costs and public services. In East and Central Africa, Ebola surveillance and cross-border measures remain important public-health concerns. Our newsroom continues to monitor developments in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Europe, Asia, Australia and Nigerian politics. Reports are attributed to their original publishers, and unverified claims are not presented as established facts.
morningSummary: Today's global briefing focuses on political accountability, public services, public health, international relations and technology. Follow the original reports linked in each story for further details and updates.
editorialNote: This is a manually prepared news edition. News can change quickly. Statements are attributed to the named speaker or publisher; summaries are not presented as direct quotations. Where a new statement or development could not be independently verified, the item is labelled accordingly. Confirm developing reports before republishing them as breaking news.

featuredStory.title: France faces renewed pressure as protest groups call for more demonstrations
featuredStory.description: French unions and protest groups have called for another nationwide demonstration on 31 October and a strike on 5 November. Reuters reports that the demonstrations have centred on wages, living costs and public services. The French Interior Ministry reported 410,000 participants in Saturday's rallies, while the CGT union gave a higher estimate. These figures come from different sources and should not be treated as identical estimates.
featuredStory.whyItMatters: The protests put pressure on the French government over the cost of living, public services and its response to public discontent.

topStories.title: Uganda tightens Ebola screening and quarantine measures
topStories.description: The Associated Press reports that Uganda has introduced stricter border measures, including health screening and a 21-day quarantine requirement for certain citizens returning from neighbouring Congo. Investigations into reported infections and possible transmission routes remain ongoing. Follow official public-health guidance for the latest information.

todaysBigQuestion.question: When governments face public anger over living costs and public services, what should come first: stronger public spending, tighter financial discipline, or a different approach to accountability?
todaysBigQuestion.context: France's demonstrations and economic pressures in many countries raise wider questions about trust, public priorities and the responsibilities of elected leaders.
todaysBigQuestion.invite: Share your view respectfully. Focus on policies, evidence and public outcomes rather than personal insults.
